sentences.text:
Writ Petition No.363 of 2025
Order:

It is stated that the petitioners are the pattadars and possessors of the various extents of agricultural land in various survey numbers situated in Jagadevpur Revenue Village and Mandal, Siddipet District and their names have been recorded in all the revenue records and they were issued pattadar passbooks under the provisions of the Telangana Rights in Land and Pattadar Passbooks Act, 2020 (for short "the Act 9 of 2020").

entities.text: Telangana Rights in Land and Pattadar Passbooks Act, 2020
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is further stated that the petitioners are receiving various incentives as investment subsidy sanctioned by the Government for cultivation of their lands.
The grievance of the petitioners is that the Irrigation Department is frequently interfering with their possession and causing inconvenience to them for enjoyment of their property.
2. Considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the respective parties and with their consent, this writ petition is disposed of at the admission stage.

3. Sri Laxmalla Sandeep, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Irrigation has placed written instructions, wherein it CVBR, J Wp_363_2025 is stated that the land in Sy.Nos.727 to 730 of Jagdevpur Village was identified on 24.07.2023 that gravel was filled and leveled which is in the foreshore area of Reddymaina Cheruvu and within the FTL limits but not carrying any type of agricultural activities.

Learned Assistant Government Pleader further submits that as per Section 24 of the Telangana Land Revenue Act, 1317 Fasli, all public roads, lanes, paths, bridges, ditches, dikes,
rivers, streams, tanks, ponds, canals, lakes and flowing water and all lands are vested with the State free from all encumbrances, if the person disputing the vesting of the property with the State, he is entitled to approach the competent civil Court for seeking declaration that he is the owner of the property.

Relying upon Section 47 of the Andhra Pradesh (Telangana Area) Irrigation Act, 1357 Fasli (for short "the Irrigation Act"), learned Assistant Government Pleader has submitted that the patta for the bed land of tank shall not be granted nor the existing occupancy rights continued where the tanks is utilized as water reservoir under a canal or channel.

entities.text: Andhra Pradesh (Telangana Area) Irrigation Act, 1357 Fasli
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
It is further stated that if the petitioners are having any valid title or pattadar passbook over the property which is forming part of the F.T.L.
of the tank, they are entitled only for compensation under the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, CVBR, J Wp_363_2025 2013 and as and when water level is being reduced they are entitled for cultivation of the subject lands and the petitioners are not entitled to fill the F.T.L. with the gravel or other mud to cause damage of full capacity of the tank and they are liable for prosecution under Section 49 of the Irrigation Act.

entities.text: Land Acquisition Act, CVBR, J Wp_363_2025 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is further submitted by the learned Assistant Government Pleader that having noticed that the petitioners are dumping the gravel in the F.T.L. of tank, the respondents are constrained to lodge complaints and the said complaints were registered as Crime Nos.39 and 156 of 2024.

sentences.text: At this stage, learned counsel for the petitioners has submitted that the petitioners being the pattadars they are entitled to cultivate the land as and when the water level is being reduced and except using the lands for cultivation, the petitioners have not caused the damage, in any manner, to the irrigation work as defined under the provisions of the Irrigation Act, and therefore, registration of crimes and also interference with the petitioners' property rights amount to violation of the rights guaranteed under Articles 14, 21 and 300-A of the Constitution of India.

Learned counsel for the petitioners further submitted without fixing the boundaries of the F.T.L. of Reddyboina Cheruvu,
the respondent authorities are not having CVBR, J Wp_363_2025 any right or authority to say that the lands which are in occupation of the petitioners are forming part of F.T.L. and they are causing damage willfully and are liable for prosecution.
5. Be that as it may, since there is a dispute with regard to the identification and localization of the lands whether the lands are patta lands of the petitioners or the same are forming part of F.T.L. of Reddymaina Cheruvu as stated by the respondents and the petitioners are intentionally causing damage to the irrigation work as defined under the Irrigation Act, these issues are required to be decided by the competent Court where the criminal cases are pending.

Since it is stated that the petitioners are pattadars and as per Section 47 of the Irrigation Act, the State is not having any power to grant patta certificates in favour of the petitioners, this Court is of the opinion that the ends of justice would be met if the joint survey is conducted by the revenue and irrigation authorities in the presence of the petitioners and fix the boundaries of the petitioners' patta lands to enable them to claim compensation either under the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 2013 or in accordance with law.
Pending conducting of such survey, the petitioners are directed not to change the nature of the land in any manner or dump gravel or mud in the subject land.

In the event of CVBR, J Wp_363_2025 violation of this order by the petitioners, the Irrigation and Revenue authorities are at liberty to take appropriate stringent action against the petitioners, in accordance with law.
6. With the above observations, this Writ Petition is disposed of.
There shall be no order as to costs.
7. As a sequel, the miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
__ JUSTICE C.V.BHASKAR REDDY 07.01.2025
